newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends more than two percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends more than two percent higher.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index closed more than two percent higher on Wednesday, as stable currencies encouraged buying of high-tech exporters.
A rally in Wall Street stocks overnight and keen interest in Japanese telecommunication shares also supported the market.
The 225-share Nikkei average surged 461.45 points or 2.32 percent to finish at 20,351.34, just below the day's high of 20.351.64. Its June futures added 540 points to end at 20,400.

"Major high-techs that posted better-than-expected earnings results, such as NEC Corp and Fujitsu Ltd, brightened the market," said Kazuo Shiogai, deputy branch manager at ING Baring Securities (Japan) Ltd.

Brokers also said the dollar's strength against the yen supported export-oriented issues. "The dollar has been quite stable above 116.00 yen, and that boosted high-techs," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
Buying in the telecommunications sector also gathered momentum, led by a rally in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), which hit a fresh high for the calendar year, brokers said.
First section turnover remained light at 374 million shares on Wednesday, although it slightly increased from Tuesday's 306 million. Gainers beat losers 836 to 254, while 143 issues were unchanged.
The broader-based TOPIX index was up 18.80 points or 1.27 percent at 1,503.25, while the Nikkei 300 average was up 3.70 points or 1.29 percent at 290.96.
Stocks posted slight gains in the morning, but were suddenly lifted in the afternoon by expectations of fresh inflows of cash from Japanese public funds, brokers also said.
High-tech shares were encouraged by the U.S. Nasdaq market's rise above the 1,400 level for the first time ever. It finished up 19 points or 1.4 percent at 1,409.
Fujitsu's shares rose 20 yen to end at 1,400. The firm was the third most heavily traded issue on the Tokyo bourse at 7.221 million shares.
NEC's shares also jumped 50 yen to end at 1,640.
Shares of Tokyo Electron Ltd hit a high for this calendar year before retracing slightly to close 170 yen higher at 5,220 yen.
"The outlook for the firm's business is not exceptionally strong, but investors think there is room for growth as the outlook for chip makers is improving," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.

Pioneer Electronic Corp rose on investors' enthusiasm in its shares after the company recently announced healthy earnings forecasts. The shares also hit a high for this calendar year before ending 120 yen higher at 2,700.
Shares of NTT closed at 1.08 million yen, up 30,000. Earlier, they hit 1.10 million yen, a high for 1997.

"There hasn't been much fresh news to stoke buying but the issue is still being powered by the company's inclusion in the Morgan Stanley Capital International's Japan index," one broker said. "Once such large issues start moving, market activity in general could pick up and the market is following NTT closely."
Robust group earnings boosted Nissan Motor Co Ltd. It ranked second on the list of heavily traded issues and rose 50 yen to close at 789.
The after-effects of a decision by Sega Enterprises Ltd and Bandai Co Ltd to cancel plans to merge were limited to the two firms, brokers said.

Sega rose 80 yen to end at 3,780, while Bandai fell 90 yen to end at 2,670. In the late afternoon, Bandai said its president Makoto Yamashina intends to resign to take responsibility for the failed merger with Sega.
The second section index was up 8.55 points at 1,771.31, with 10.52 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 1.79 points at 1,181.79.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
